context.title: Abimelech's Bloody Reign
context.summary: Gideon's son Abimelech kills seventy of his brothers and is made king at Shechem. The one survivor, Jotham, tells a fable about trees choosing a bramble as king. Within three years Shechem and Abimelech destroy each other.
context.background: Abimelech appealed to his mother's kin in Shechem (vv. 1–3), a city with Canaanite roots and a temple of Baal-berith, 'lord of the covenant,' which funded his hired thugs (v. 4). Jotham's fable shows useful trees refusing to rule while a worthless bramble promises shade it cannot give. Abimelech's death by a woman's millstone was remembered generations later (2 Samuel 11:21).

customs.note: Scattering salt over a destroyed city was a symbolic curse, marking it as a place of lasting desolation.
The upper stone of a hand mill, which women used daily to grind grain.

watchFor: Seventy pieces of silver for seventy murders (vv. 4–5).
Abimelech dies trying to hide that a woman killed him (v. 54).

people.name: Gideon
people.summary: Called also Jerubbaal (Judg. 6:29, 32), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8). His calling is the commencement of the second period in the history of the judges.

people.name: Abimelech
people.summary: A son of Gideon (Judg. 9:1), who was proclaimed king after the death of his father (Judg. 8:33-9:6). One of his first acts was to murder his brothers, seventy in number, “on one stone,” at Ophrah.

people.name: Jotham
people.summary: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26; comp. Gen. 35:4) “that was in Shechem, to make Abimelech king,” from one of the heights of Mount Gerizim he protested against their doing so in the earliest parable, that of the bramble-king.

people.name: Midian
people.summary: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Gaal
people.summary: Loathing, the son of Ebed, in whom the Shechemites “placed their confidence” when they became discontented with Abimelech. He headed the revolution, and led out the men of Shechem against Abimelech; but was defeated, and fled to his own home (Judg. 9:26-46).

people.name: Ebed
people.summary: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

people.name: Shechem
people.summary: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

people.name: Hamor
people.summary: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16.

people.name: Zebul
people.summary: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech (Judg. 9:28, 30, 36). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: A city in Samaria (Gen. 33:18), called also Sichem (12:6), Sychem (Acts 7:16). It stood in the narrow sheltered valley between Ebal on the north and Gerizim on the south, these mountains at their base being only some 500 yards apart.

places.name: Ophrah
places.summary: “Of the Abi-ezrites.” A city of Manasseh, 6 miles south-west of Shechem, the residence of Gideon (Judg. 6:11; 8:27, 32). After his great victory over the Midianites, he slew at this place the captive kings (8:18-21).

places.name: Beth-millo
places.summary: In Judg. 9:6, 20 it is the name of a rampart in Shechem, probably the “tower of Shechem” (9:46, 49).

places.name: mount Gerizim
places.summary: A mountain of Samaria, about 3,000 feet above the Mediterranean. It was on the left of the valley containing the ancient town of Shechem, on the way to Jerusalem.

places.name: Lebanon
places.summary: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria. It is a branch running southward from the Caucasus, and at its lower end forking into two parallel ranges, the eastern or Anti-Lebanon, and the western or Lebanon proper.

places.name: Midian
places.summary: An Arabian tribe descended from Midian. They inhabited principally the desert north of the peninsula of Arabia. The peninsula of Sinai was the pasture-ground for their flocks.

places.name: Beer
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Judah to which Jotham fled for fear of Abimelech (Judg. 9:21).

places.name: Diviners' Oak
places.summary: (Judg. 9:37; A.V., “the plain of Meonenim;” R.V., “the oak of Meonenim”) means properly “soothsayers” or “sorcerers,” “wizards” (Deut. 18:10, 14; 2 Kings 21:6; Micah 5:12).

places.name: mount Zalmon
places.summary: Shady; or Zalmon, a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48).

places.name: Thebez
places.summary: Brightness, a place some 11 miles north-east of Shechem, on the road to Scythopolis, the modern Tabas.

events.title: Usurpation by Abimelech
events.summary: Passage: Judges 8:29–9:57. People: Abimelech. Place: Canaan. Lasted about 3 years.
